newsitem.title: CHINA: Apstar 2R to be launched in late Aug-APT.
newsitem.headline: Apstar 2R to be launched in late Aug-APT.

text.p: Beijing-controlled Hong Kong firm APT Satellite Holdings Ltd said on Monday its Apstar 2R satellite is expected to be launched at the end of August.
"According to the schedule we've set with China Great Wall, up to this moment, the launch date is the end of August," APT spokesman Brian Lo told Reuters.

China Great Wall Industry Corp is a Chinese state-run company that handles commercial space launch contracts with foreign firms. China will use a new-generation Long March 3B rocket to launch communications satellite Apstar 2R.
A Chinese official said last month the satellite will be launched after August.
But Lo said the latest scheduled launch date had been postponed from the original target in the middle of the year because China wanted more time for testing the rocket to improve its reliability.
He acknowledged the delay would also mean a corresponding postponement in income, but added it was not a major delay.
The utilisation rate of Apstar 2R transponders is over 30 percent, and is expected to increase to 50 to 60 percent by the end of the year, Lo said.
